name.description: Return labels with this name, compared case-insensitively. Create and update apply the same case-insensitive rule, so use this filter to check for a label before you create one.

name-in.description: Return labels whose name is in this comma-separated list: `?name__in=Roadmap,Platform`. This match is case-sensitive.

search.description: A search term matched against the label name.

order-by.description: Field to sort by. Prefix with `-` for descending. Defaults to `sort_order`. - `sort_order`, `-sort_order` - `name`, `-name` - `created_at`, `-created_at` - `id`, `-id`

offset.description: Number of rows to skip from the start of the result set. Maximum 10000. Use the `next` value from the response instead of computing offsets yourself.

paginate.description: Set to `cursor` to switch to the keyset envelope (no `COUNT` query), which returns `next_cursor` and `has_more` instead of `next` and `total_count`. Cursor pagination needs `order_by` set to `created_at`, `-created_at`, `id`, or `-id`. Any other ordering, including the default `sort_order`, returns `400 ordering_not_cursor_eligible`.

count.description: Defaults to `true`. Set to `false` to skip the `COUNT(*)` behind `total_count`. The response then omits `total_count`.

fields.description: Comma-separated list of fields to return on each row. Fields you don't request are left out of the response instead of coming back as `null`, so a missing key means you didn't ask for it and `null` means the value is null. `id` is always included, whether or not you name it. Pass `all` to get every requestable field. An unknown field name returns `400` with the list of valid names and the closest match, so a typo is caught instead of being silently ignored. Requestable here: `color`, `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `description`, `id`, `name`, `sort_order`, `updated_at`, `updated_by_id`. See [Sparse fields](/api-reference/v2/sparse-fields).
